samples.summary: Internal-paste provenance is decided by clipboard-text equality, and the change extends the buffer's lifetime indefinitely, widening the window in which foreign clipboard content is treated as internally-originated
samples.evidence: `paste` decides an internal paste with `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2243) — content equality, not provenance. The diff removes `clearCopyBuffer()` from both view paste paths (view/worksheet.ts:4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:728), so a non-cut buffer now survives for the whole session until Escape. Vector: a page the user copies from (a `copy`-event override or any site that seeds the clipboard) that emits text identical to what is still buffered — trivially reachable for small single-cell copies such as `10` — makes the engine take the internal branch. That branch skips `applyInputInferenceToGrid` and now additionally re-creates the buffered merge blocks, drops destination blocks it fully covers (`applyPasteMerges`, sheet.ts:2519) and clears cells under the new blocks (`clearCellsUnderMerge`, sheet.ts:2564). The user sees one thing on the clipboard and the sheet writes another, including structural merge changes and cell deletions. No attacker-controlled bytes are written (the grid comes from the buffer), which is why I rate this minor rather than an injection, but the trust decision is made on attacker-influenceable input and the window got much larger.

samples.summary: Copy buffer holding a full snapshot of copied cell values, formulas, styles and merges is now retained for the session lifetime with no clearing on paste
samples.evidence: Both view paste paths dropped their `this.sheet.clearCopyBuffer()` call (view/worksheet.ts:4947 and view/spreadsheet.ts:728). `copyBuffer` (sheet.ts:~375) holds `grid`, `rangeStyles`, `merges` and the raw `text` of the copied region. Only `Sheet.paste` clears it, and only for a consumed cut (sheet.ts:2286); otherwise it is cleared solely by the Escape key rule (view/worksheet.ts:5118). Nothing clears it on blur, on a read-only transition, or on teardown, so a copy of sensitive cells stays resident in the page's heap indefinitely and is recoverable from any heap snapshot or later in-page script execution. Hardening: clear the buffer alongside the existing Escape handler on document/tab teardown, and on a read-only transition.

samples.summary: New paste path amplifies an unvalidated remote MergeSpan into O(rs×cs) sequential store reads, adding a client-hang amplification site
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` iterates `mergeCoveredSrefs(anchor, span)` (sheet.ts:2572) doing an `await this.store.get(ref)` per covered cell, and `applyPasteMerges` calls it once per pasted block. `span` ultimately originates from `this.merges`, loaded verbatim from the collaborative document (`loadMerges`, sheet.ts:545 → `YorkieStore.getMerges`, yorkie-store.ts:1010, which only spreads `{...span}` with no bound check on `rs`/`cs`). A malicious collaborator or a crafted imported document can therefore place a block with an enormous span; a subsequent copy+paste of a region containing it turns into a multi-million-iteration awaited loop that freezes the tab. I note this as pre-existing in kind — `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:818) already walks every covered cell on load, and `moveRangeTo` had the same loop — so the diff adds an amplification site rather than the root cause. The fix belongs at ingestion: validate/clamp `rs`/`cs` when merges are read from the store.

samples.summary: The newly added merge-structure writes in paste have no model- or store-level read-only guard; enforcement rests entirely on the two view call sites plus the server webhook
samples.evidence: `Sheet.paste` guards only `this.pivotDefinition` (sheet.ts:2217) and then writes merge structure via `store.setMerge` / `store.deleteMerge` (sheet.ts:2538, 2543). `Sheet` has no read-only notion, and `YorkieStore` — created with the read-only flag at sheet-view.tsx:1012 — does not honour it in `setMerge`/`deleteMerge` (yorkie-store.ts:961, 984); its `readOnly` only silences three other writes (651, 689, 1311). I traced every caller and found none unguarded (worksheet.ts:5141 and spreadsheet.ts:699 both return on read-only), and the Yorkie auth webhook refuses a viewer's PushPull server-side by default (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29), so this is not currently bypassable — it is defence-in-depth: any future caller of `Sheet.paste` (an API surface, a harness bridge, a mobile handler) inherits no gate.
